title: micro-debrief-runtime-handoff-maya-singh
content:
Candidate: Jordan Vega
Role: Senior Runtime Engineer (inference serving)
Interviewer: Maya Singh (owner), Aria Patel, Noah Kim
Interview date: 2026-02-26
Loop summary (quick): Jordan is strong on low-level performance debugging and kernel-level intuition, weaker on API/consumption ergonomics and cross-team communication. Did well on latency root-cause examples; struggled to describe a pragmatic rollout strategy for multi-model fallback under constrained capacity.

Quick scores (my view):
- System design / architecture: 4/5 — solid latency-first mental model, good trade-offs for batching and KV cache; clear about trade-offs between prefix cache and memory pressure.
- Coding / implementation: 3/5 — clean code in pairing exercise but missed an edge-case for concurrent cache invalidation; needed prompting on thread-safety primitives.
- Production judgment / ops: 3.5/5 — knows SRE basics, less comfortable with infra-as-code choices and migration planning.
- Communication & onboarding: 3/5 — explains concepts well to peers, but answers to cross-team stakeholder questions were terse.
- Overall fit for senior IC: 3.5/5

Notable strengths (bullets):
- Deep troubleshooting examples: traced a 60% p99 regression to a tensor copy site; comfortable reading disassembler-like traces and profiling flamegraphs.
- Hands-on with kernel tuning: talked about fused attention kernels and memory layout impacts in real systems.
- Empathetic to infra cost: suggested sensible batching heuristics tied to expected sequence length distributions rather than fixed batch sizes.

Risks / concerns (bullets):
- Limited experience owning customer-facing APIs (we need someone who can bake ops into product-facing SLAs).
- Pairing exercise revealed gaps in concurrency control under cache eviction pressure — potential source of flakiness if unchecked.
- Communication: will need coaching on stakeholder communication & trade-off framing when negotiating rollout windows.

Open/ follow-up questions (to ask in reference checks or follow-up interview):
- Concrete examples of deploying model fallbacks across regions (did they actually run a canary->fallback flow or just whiteboard it?).
- Direct familiarity with Triton / TorchScript / Onnxruntime? They mentioned fragments but not sustained ownership.
- Experience with quantized kernels in production (8-bit/4-bit): has toy projects but unclear on end-to-end accuracy/regression testing practices.

Suggested interview follow-up (if we want to dig deeper):
- Short take-home: design a simple rollout plan for degrading from an H100-optimized model to a quantized A100 variant, include tracing & alerting hooks (48h).
- Reference call: ask former manager specifically about ownership of rollout incidents and communication with product/SRE.

Recommendation and proposed hire action:
- Recommendation: Hire (level: Senior IC) with structured onboarding and a 6-month focused probation. Candidate brings strong low-level chops we need; we should mitigate the communication and production-ops gaps via a targeted ramp plan.

Proposed 6-month probation / success plan (measurable bullets):
1) Month 0–1: Core onboarding + pair with kernel team on a small (non-user-facing) perf fix. Deliverable: one PR improving memory layout for an attention kernel; reviewer: Aria.
2) Month 1–3: Lead a small rollout (internal test-only) of a batched KV cache optimization with end-to-end tracing added. Deliverable: runbook + postmortem + perf dashboard card. Success metric: no more than 1 P0 caused by rollout, latency p99 improvement >= 10% on target route.
3) Month 3–6: Own one cross-functional migration: shepherd a model-variant fallback policy from canary to prod across two regions. Deliverable: rollout plan, alerting thresholds, and a 1-page stakeholder comms template. Success metric: zero customer-facing incidents and documented rollback criteria.
4) Mentorship / comms: bi-weekly 1:1 with Eng Manager + monthly skip-level with PM to practice framing trade-offs and stakeholder updates.

Onboarding tickets (suggested initial tasks):
- RUNTIME-6001: Readme: how we do prefix caching (assign to Jordan, due week1)
- RUNTIME-6004: Pair PR for kernel memory touches (week2)
- RUNTIME-6012: Add tracing spans to fallback router (month1)

Comp concerns / leveling notes:
- Strong domain expertise aligns to Senior; consider salary band toward lower-mid of senior given production-ops gap. If references highlight stronger ownership, revisit.

Notes to self (informal):
- If we hire: schedule a focused week-2 shadow on release window comms.
- Keep the take-home narrow and deadline-tight to avoid candidate over-investing.
- Flag for hiring committee: needs explicit support for stakeholder communication — add a coaching package in offer.

Raw pairing snippets (copied quickly):
- When asked about cache eviction, Jordan: "I would hold a lock for the bucket, do eviction synchronously, then release" — asked about contention, responded "we can sharded locks" but didn't discuss backpressure.
- On rollback: "we push a canary and watch traces" — asked what traces/metrics are essential; candidate listed latency, error rate, and queue depth but didn't propose SLO thresholds.

Decision box (my pick): "Hire with structured onboarding + 6mo probation focused on ops/comms"

Action items (immediate):
- [ ] Share this note with Aria + Noah for quick comments (48h)
- [ ] Send take-home if exec ok (deadline 3 days)
- [ ] If positive refs, prepare draft offer template including coaching clause
